significance.root_decision: For every n and every row-stochastic n x n matrix A with n distinct eigenvalues, A has the global anti-diagonal eigenvalue property (every leading block is lower triangular and real diagonalizable, and the eigenvalues of the block times the reversal matrix are the signed diagonal entries with multiplicity) if and only if A is a binomial transform B Diag(a) B^{-1} of some vector a. This is Conjecture 2.6 of Britnell and Wildon. The source proves the easy direction, the converse away from an exceptional algebraic set, and the cases n <= 4. The proof here is by induction on the size: a maximum principle for iterated finite differences of the eigenvectors forces them into a polynomial flag when the last parameter is positive, and a determinant identity excludes the remaining zero case because it would repeat an eigenvalue. Lean states the property block by block as the conjecture does, not through the eigenbasis property of the source's Theorem 2.9, and assumes no moment representation.
significance.caveat: Bounded literature search only. The proof is about one page built on the source's own Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.3, and its maximum-principle idea is natural, so a specialist could call it a neat short proof of a conjecture the authors verified only for n <= 4 (cross-model confidence: not routine 0.65, not public 0.85). One reading choice: 'distinct eigenvalues' is applied to the matrix L itself, which the source's sentence before the conjecture supports; a probe of 1,474 structured cases found no counterexample under the other reading either. Closest unpublished related work: Ochiai, Sasada, Shirai and Tsuboi, arXiv:1403.6797.
